newsitem.title: USA: Tribune operating income up on publishing, TV results.
newsitem.headline: Tribune operating income up on publishing, TV results.

text.p: Tribune Co., publisher of the Chicago Tribune, said Friday its operating income soared in the first quarter as publishing profits jumped 51 percent and its television stations had their best quarter ever.
Net income from continuing operations rose 28 percent in the quarter ended March 30 to $65 million, or 49 cents a share, from $50 million, or 37 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
The company said the latest results excluded Tribune's holdings in Quno Corp., a newsprint manufacturer, which it sold in March 1996 for a gain of $89 million.
Tribune's performance improved mainly because of a 51 percent gain in publishing profits. Operating revenues grew to $593.9 million from $537.1 million.

"Our publishing group had an exceptionally strong first quarter with better than expected revenue growth coupled with lower newsprint prices," said John Madigan, Tribune's chairman, president and chief executive.
"And our television stations had a record first quarter. We closed our largest acquisition ever in late March, creating the nation's No. 2 broadcasting group."
Tribune said operating profit from its publishing business rose to $95 million from $63 million, due mainly to higher advertising revenues and lower newsprint prices.

Publishing revenues increased 8 percent to $355 million. Advertising revenues rose 10 percent due to higher rates and linage, with retail advertising up 6 percent, general advertising up 8 percent and classified up 13 percent.
Newsprint and ink expenses dropped 28 percent in the quarter. Average newsprint prices were down about 30 percent from 1996, while consumption rose 5 percent.
Other publishing expenses were up 7 percent, mainly due to higher compensation costs and increased development of Internet businesses, Tribune said.

Tribune said its operating profit from broadcasting and entertainment rose 2 percent to a record $30 million from $29 million. Operating profits from its 16 television stations rose 23 percent to a record $31 million.

This was partially offset, however, by an equity loss of $11 million in the WB Network, compared with a loss of $3 million in 1996. Tribune increased its stake in the network to 21.9 percent from 12.5 percent in the 1997 first quarter.
Operating revenues for broadcasting and entertainment rose 8 percent, to $201 million from $187 million a year ago, due mainly to a 9 percent increase from television, Tribune said.

Television gains were attributed primarily to improvement in Chicago and the acquisition of six television stations from Renaissance Communications last month and of KSWB-San Diego in April 1996. Excluding acquisitions, television revenues rose 5 percent.
Tribune said its education division had an operating loss of $200,000 in the first quarter, compared with a year-ago profit of $2.2 million.
The loss was due primarily to acquisitions of Educational Publishing Corp. and NTC Publishing Group in March 1996, Tribune said.
Tribune's stock rose 50 cents to $41.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
